dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a natural number n, this is the type Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) Real, definitionally the function type Fin n -> Fin n -> Real.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes A and B square n-by-n matrices with real entries.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002
dependency_coverage.meaning: This maps a square real matrix A to Norm.norm A using the Norm component of Matrix.frobeniusNormedRing.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the real-valued matrix norm applied to A, B, and their product in the inequality.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef003
dependency_coverage.meaning: For square matrices A and B, it defines a matrix C by C(i,j) = sum over all k in Fin n of A(i,k) * B(k,j).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The matrix inside the norm on the left-hand side is the usual finite matrix product of A and B.

dependency_coverage.name: HMul.hMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is the operation extracted from a heterogeneous-multiplication structure.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: With the supplied real multiplication instances, it denotes ordinary real multiplication both in each matrix-product summand and between the two norm values.

dependency_coverage.name: LE.le
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is the binary relation extracted from an LE structure.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Instantiated with Real.instLE, it makes the target conclusion a non-strict inequality between real numbers.

dependency_coverage.name: Nat
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is the type of natural numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The matrix dimension n ranges over every natural number, including zero.

dependency_coverage.name: Real
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is the type of real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Matrix entries and all norm values in the target are real numbers.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instLE
dependency_coverage.meaning: This equips the real numbers with their usual less-than-or-equal relation.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It interprets the target relation as the ordinary real inequality <=.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: This equips the real numbers with ordinary real multiplication.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It determines the scalar products A(i,k) * B(k,j) and the product of the two norm values on the right-hand side.

dependency_coverage.name: instHMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: Given a multiplication operation on a type, this constructs homogeneous heterogeneous multiplication by using that same operation.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It turns Real.instMul into the HMul operation used by the target and by the explicitly defined matrix product.

dependency_coverage.name: Fin
dependency_coverage.meaning: Fin n is the finite index type with n elements, conventionally represented by the natural numbers from 0 through n-1.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the row, column, and contracted inner indices of the n-by-n matrices.

dependency_coverage.name: Fin.fintype
dependency_coverage.meaning: This gives Fin n its finite enumeration, built from the list of indices in finRange n.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It permits the universal finite set of inner indices to be formed and summed over; it also supports construction of the matrix norm instance.

dependency_coverage.name: Finset.sum
dependency_coverage.meaning: This forms the finite sum of a function's values in an additive commutative monoid.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It adds the terms A(i,k) * B(k,j) to compute each entry of the product matrix.

dependency_coverage.name: Finset.univ
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a finite type, this is the finite set containing every element of that type.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes the contracted sum range over every k in Fin n, with no omitted indices.

dependency_coverage.name: Matrix
dependency_coverage.meaning: A matrix with row type m, column type n, and entries in alpha is definitionally a function m -> n -> alpha.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It gives the matrices their entrywise functional representation and, with both index types equal to Fin n, makes them square.

dependency_coverage.name: Matrix.frobeniusNormedRing
dependency_coverage.meaning: This constructs a NormedRing structure on square matrices over an RCLike scalar type. Its Norm component is inherited from Matrix.frobeniusSeminormedAddCommGroup, while its ring operations are inherited from Matrix.instRing. The inherited norm's defining formula is not supplied in the dossier.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Only its inherited Norm component is extracted in the target, selecting the matrix norm denoted by N_n below.

dependency_coverage.name: Norm.norm
dependency_coverage.meaning: This extracts the real-valued norm function from a Norm structure.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It evaluates the selected matrix norm on A, B, and the explicitly defined product matrix.

dependency_coverage.name: NormedRing.toNorm
dependency_coverage.meaning: This extracts the Norm component of a NormedRing structure.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It connects Matrix.frobeniusNormedRing to the norm function used by LocalDef002.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instAddCommMonoid
dependency_coverage.meaning: This supplies real addition, zero, and the additive commutative-monoid laws.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It determines how the finite matrix-product sums are added and makes an empty sum equal to real zero.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instRCLike
dependency_coverage.meaning: This gives the real numbers their RCLike structure, with zero imaginary part and the usual real normed-field structure.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It specializes the matrix NormedRing construction to real matrices and introduces no additional proposition-level hypothesis.

dependency_coverage.name: instDecidableEqFin
dependency_coverage.meaning: This decides equality of two Fin n indices by deciding equality of their underlying natural-number values.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is computational structure required to construct the matrix NormedRing instance; it imposes no extra mathematical restriction.

binders: n is an implicitly bound, universally quantified natural number.
A and B are universally quantified square n-by-n matrices with real entries, equivalently functions Fin n -> Fin n -> Real.
conclusions: If C is defined entrywise by C(i,j) = sum_{k in Fin n} A(i,k) * B(k,j), then N_n(C) <= N_n(A) * N_n(B).
mathematical_definitions: Let I_n = Fin n, the n-element index set.
Let M_n(R) be the set of functions I_n -> I_n -> R.
For A,B in M_n(R), define their product C by C(i,j) = sum_{k in I_n} A(i,k)B(k,j).
Define N_n(A) to be the norm of A selected by the Norm component of Matrix.frobeniusNormedRing.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every natural number n and every pair of real n-by-n matrices A and B, the selected matrix norm of their ordinary matrix product is at most the product of their selected matrix norms. The multiplicative bound has exact constant 1 and has no assumptions on A or B.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The statement concerns only finite square matrices over the real numbers; it does not directly quantify over rectangular or complex matrices.
The dimension n is not required to be positive. For n = 0 there is a unique empty matrix, every product-entry sum is empty, and the case is degenerate rather than logically vacuous.
There are no premises, so the proposition cannot hold merely through inconsistent or unsatisfied assumptions.
The product is defined using exact finite sums and exact real arithmetic; no floating-point computation, rounding model, or approximation error is encoded.
The conclusion contains one non-strict inequality and no conjunction, existential witness, equality characterization, optimality claim, or reverse bound.
No invertibility, symmetry, positivity, rank, or nonzero condition is imposed on either matrix.
ambiguities: The supplied body of Matrix.frobeniusNormedRing delegates its norm to Matrix.frobeniusSeminormedAddCommGroup, whose definition is absent. Consequently, the dossier alone does not justify replacing N_n(A) by a particular closed formula such as sqrt(sum_{i,j} A(i,j)^2), nor does it expose any possible normalization. Retaining N_n as the exact instance-selected norm is therefore the fully supported translation.
